criteria.rationale: I'm ruling Judge A's fail. The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates from its old state to its new state in place. The guidance says to judge the kit's ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Only primitives that carry a shared `layoutId` can carry an entity across that remount. MotionNode does (MotionNode.tsx:14-16). The kit's Arrow primitive does not. It takes an identity `id` but only writes it to `data-presentation-id` (Arrow.tsx:62-63). It never sets `layoutId` or `layout`. Its geometry is animated only by the `d` interpolation on `motion.path` with `initial={false}` (Arrow.tsx:76-79), which can only interpolate while the same component instance stays mounted. Across an ungrouped transition, the incoming Arrow is a fresh instance. Its paths start at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T (Arrow.tsx:70-73). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. That is the 'vanishes and reappears instead of morphing' failure the guidance names, so the clause 'animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place' is unmet for Arrow entities. Judges B and C are right that Stage uses sync mode with no mode="wait", that the exiting wrapper is taken out of flow, and that MotionNode has no opacity hiding or delay. But they judged only the MotionNode-based primitives. They never looked at Arrow, which is also a kit entity primitive with a stable id. A pass needs every primitive that renders a persisting entity to keep it visible and morph it, so their reasoning does not decide the requirement. Arrow fails it. The delivered sample puts all nine steps in one group (steps/index.ts:7-12), but that does not change the kit behavior this criterion targets: the guidance explicitly names the ungrouped transition.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: The fit scale is computed from the measured stage area, which is the box the stage actually occupies. A single factor, the minimum of w/designW and h/designH, is applied to both axes via transform: scale(). Header, footer and ToC are siblings outside the measured area, so the canvas is bounded by what remains.
evidence: useFitScale measures areaRef.getBoundingClientRect() with a ResizeObserver (resize-listener fallback) and calls computeFitScale(width, height, mode, designW, designH).

Stage applies transform `translate(-50%,-50%) scale(${scale})` to a fixed designW x designH element inside an overflow:hidden area, so the internal composition does not reflow.
The area is flex 1 1 0 with minHeight 0, so the chrome is excluded from it. At 1280x720 and 390x844 the scale derives from the measured area, not the window.

criteria.rationale: I'm ruling with judge B (pass). The three clauses hold. (1) Typed props: every public primitive exported from index.ts has an explicit typed interface. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use NodeProps (id: string, at?: At, className?: string, style?: CSSProperties, variant?: string, children?: ReactNode). Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use ArrowProps, AppearProps and SceneLayerProps. None is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, which is the fail trigger the guidance names for this clause. (2) Identity hooks cannot be overridden: MotionNode destructures a fixed set of fields and builds layoutId, data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and data-variant itself, with no caller spread on the rendered element. Arrow and SceneLayer set their data-presentation-* hooks directly. SceneLayer spreads only the caller's style object. Appear accepts no caller element props. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: `at` is used only by placement(); Box pulls `Icon` out and renders it as a child; `kind` and `tag` are used only to pick the hook value and the element; Arrow's from, to, bend, bidirectional, designW and designH go into path math and sizing. Judge A fails clause 1 because the interfaces are bespoke rather than inherited element props. The guidance's trigger for that clause is an untyped bag in place of the element's props, and it says typed primitives that apply hooks safely and strip kit-only props pass. A hand-written typed interface is not an untyped bag, so A's reason does not decide the requirement. Judge C says Box's `{...props}` after `kind="box"` lets a caller override data-presentation-node. Box's rest props are typed as NodeProps minus Icon and children, and NodeProps has no `kind` or `tag` field. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip likewise take only NodeProps, so TypeScript's JSX excess-property check rejects a caller passing `kind`. No source in the candidate passes it, so C's scenario is a hypothetical input the cited source does not produce. Also, layoutId and data-presentation-id are written inside MotionNode with no caller spread after them.

Those facts are accurate, but they don't answer the deciding majority reason, which concerns the kit's Arrow primitive. That reason holds up in the material. In an ungrouped transition, Stage keys the scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id`, so the incoming step mounts a new Scene instance. Arrow is a kit entity primitive that takes an identity `id`, but it writes that id only to `data-presentation-id`. It never sets `layout` or `layoutId`, so nothing carries it across the remount. Its `motion.path` elements use `initial={false}` and interpolate `d` only within one mounted instance. The new Arrow therefore starts at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T while the old copy fades out with the exiting scene. So an Arrow entity with the same id in two consecutive ungrouped steps does not animate from its old endpoints to its new ones in place. The old copy fades out and a new copy fades in. That leaves the requirement clause "animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place" unmet for Arrow entities. The dissent never examines Arrow, so the material refutes its pass.

result.rationale: I'm ruling Judge A's fail. The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates from its old state to its new state in place. The guidance says to judge the kit's ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Only primitives that carry a shared `layoutId` can carry an entity across that remount. MotionNode does (MotionNode.tsx:14-16). The kit's Arrow primitive does not. It takes an identity `id` but only writes it to `data-presentation-id` (Arrow.tsx:62-63). It never sets `layoutId` or `layout`. Its geometry is animated only by the `d` interpolation on `motion.path` with `initial={false}` (Arrow.tsx:76-79), which can only interpolate while the same component instance stays mounted. Across an ungrouped transition, the incoming Arrow is a fresh instance. Its paths start at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T (Arrow.tsx:70-73). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. That is the 'vanishes and reappears instead of morphing' failure the guidance names, so the clause 'animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place' is unmet for Arrow entities. Judges B and C are right that Stage uses sync mode with no mode="wait", that the exiting wrapper is taken out of flow, and that MotionNode has no opacity hiding or delay. But they judged only the MotionNode-based primitives. They never looked at Arrow, which is also a kit entity primitive with a stable id. A pass needs every primitive that renders a persisting entity to keep it visible and morph it, so their reasoning does not decide the requirement. Arrow fails it. The delivered sample puts all nine steps in one group (steps/index.ts:7-12), but that does not change the kit behavior this criterion targets: the guidance explicitly names the ungrouped transition.

Arrow and SceneLayer set their data-presentation-* hooks directly. Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Box pulls out `Icon`, MotionNode uses `at` only in placement() and uses `kind`/`tag` only to pick the hook value and the element, and Arrow uses its geometry props only in path math. checks.rationale: The dissent's reason is that Box spreads `{...props}` after `kind="box"`, so a caller could override the `data-presentation-node` hook. The source doesn't support this. In `src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx`, the rest object is typed from `BoxProps extends NodeProps` with `Icon` and `children` taken out. `NodeProps` in `src/presentation-kit/nodes/types.ts` declares only `id`, `at`, `className`, `style`, `variant` and `children`. It has no `kind` or `tag`. A typed caller therefore has no field in that spread that could replace `kind`. Also, the spread goes onto MotionNode, not onto a DOM element. `src/presentation-kit/nodes/MotionNode.tsx` builds `layoutId`, `data-presentation-node`, `data-presentation-id` and `data-variant` itself from destructured fields, and spreads no caller props onto the rendered `motion.div` or `motion.span`. The other wrappers (Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip) work the same way: they take only `NodeProps`, so `kind` cannot reach them through their typed props. The override needs a caller to pass `kind` against the types. No delivered source does that, so it is a hypothetical input and does not show the identity-hook clause unmet.

result.rationale: I'm ruling with judge B (pass). The three clauses hold. (1) Typed props: every public primitive exported from index.ts has an explicit typed interface. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use NodeProps (id: string, at?: At, className?: string, style?: CSSProperties, variant?: string, children?: ReactNode). Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use ArrowProps, AppearProps and SceneLayerProps. None is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, which is the fail trigger the guidance names for this clause. (2) Identity hooks cannot be overridden: MotionNode destructures a fixed set of fields and builds layoutId, data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and data-variant itself, with no caller spread on the rendered element. Arrow and SceneLayer set their data-presentation-* hooks directly. SceneLayer spreads only the caller's style object. Appear accepts no caller element props. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: `at` is used only by placement(); Box pulls `Icon` out and renders it as a child; `kind` and `tag` are used only to pick the hook value and the element; Arrow's from, to, bend, bidirectional, designW and designH go into path math and sizing. Judge A fails clause 1 because the interfaces are bespoke rather than inherited element props. The guidance's trigger for that clause is an untyped bag in place of the element's props, and it says typed primitives that apply hooks safely and strip kit-only props pass. A hand-written typed interface is not an untyped bag, so A's reason does not decide the requirement. Judge C says Box's `{...props}` after `kind="box"` lets a caller override data-presentation-node. Box's rest props are typed as NodeProps minus Icon and children, and NodeProps has no `kind` or `tag` field. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip likewise take only NodeProps, so TypeScript's JSX excess-property check rejects a caller passing `kind`. No source in the candidate passes it, so C's scenario is a hypothetical input the cited source does not produce. Also, layoutId and data-presentation-id are written inside MotionNode with no caller spread after them.

checks.rationale: The material does not show that this timeout path leaves the preview server running. In `tests/integration/helpers.ts`, `exec()` sends SIGKILL to the npm child only when the 280 s timer fires. Killing npm with SIGKILL does not pass a signal on to its children. The orphaned `node scripts/verify.mjs` process therefore keeps running instead of being killed. The auditor says the script's finally cleanup never runs, but that does not follow. After the preview starts, every wait in `verify.mjs` has a bound: readiness has a 30 s deadline, `waitForSelector` 10 s, step transitions 4 s, text reads 2 s, and Playwright's default navigation timeout applies. Every exit path then reaches `finally { await browser?.close(); preview.stop() }`, and `stop()` kills the detached process group with `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL')`. Also, `exec()` resolves on the child's 'close' event, which waits until all inherited stdio pipes close. In practice that means the test waits for the orphaned verify process to finish. This timeout is also a hypothetical exit path that the recorded runs never hit. The guidance's failure case is a test that kills only the wrapper and leaves the preview running, and the material does not show that outcome. The tests that start previews themselves use `freePort()` for dynamic ports. `sample-scene.test.ts` stops its preview process group in `afterAll`. `verify-failures.test.ts` asserts after each pristine and fault run that no `vite.js` processes remain. scene-kit.rationale: Stage uses AnimatePresence in default sync mode, not wait. Every entity in the sample Scene, including nested Labels, is rendered inside an Appear group.

contradiction.rationale: The primary fails this solely because the props are bespoke interfaces rather than element-prop inheritance. The guidance's fail trigger for the first clause is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, and none of these primitives uses one. Each is an explicit typed interface (NodeProps, ArrowProps, AppearProps, SceneLayerProps). The other two clauses are met, as the primary itself concedes. MotionNode destructures explicit fields and sets data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and layoutId without spreading caller props, so callers cannot override identity hooks. Kit-only props (Icon, at, variant) are not forwarded to the DOM. No clause in the guidance is triggered, so the fail is not supported.

first_results.rationale: I'm ruling Judge A's fail. The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates from its old state to its new state in place. The guidance says to judge the kit's ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Only primitives that carry a shared `layoutId` can carry an entity across that remount. MotionNode does (MotionNode.tsx:14-16). The kit's Arrow primitive does not. It takes an identity `id` but only writes it to `data-presentation-id` (Arrow.tsx:62-63). It never sets `layoutId` or `layout`. Its geometry is animated only by the `d` interpolation on `motion.path` with `initial={false}` (Arrow.tsx:76-79), which can only interpolate while the same component instance stays mounted. Across an ungrouped transition, the incoming Arrow is a fresh instance. Its paths start at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T (Arrow.tsx:70-73). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. That is the 'vanishes and reappears instead of morphing' failure the guidance names, so the clause 'animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place' is unmet for Arrow entities. Judges B and C are right that Stage uses sync mode with no mode="wait", that the exiting wrapper is taken out of flow, and that MotionNode has no opacity hiding or delay. But they judged only the MotionNode-based primitives. They never looked at Arrow, which is also a kit entity primitive with a stable id. A pass needs every primitive that renders a persisting entity to keep it visible and morph it, so their reasoning does not decide the requirement. Arrow fails it. The delivered sample puts all nine steps in one group (steps/index.ts:7-12), but that does not change the kit behavior this criterion targets: the guidance explicitly names the ungrouped transition.
evidence: Stage.tsx:28 keys the scene by `step.groupKey ?? step.id`, so ungrouped consecutive steps remount separate scene instances.
Stage.tsx:51-59: sync-mode AnimatePresence. The new scene fades in from opacity 0 while the old scene exits with opacity 0, position absolute and inset 0.
MotionNode.tsx:14-16 gives Box, Label and the other MotionNode wrappers `layout` and `layoutId: id`, the only way an entity can carry across scene instances.
Arrow.tsx:61-74: the Arrow svg has no layoutId or layout. `id` is used only as data-presentation-id. The svg starts at opacity 0 and fades in over ENTER_T (0.4s, constants.ts:10).

first_results.rationale: `diagnose()` in scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs runs on every settled step. It collects a box for each element that has its own visible text, plus every chrome element matched by `chromeSel`: marker, deck-title, step-title, caption, prev, next, dots, toc and attribution (lines 56-59). Chrome elements are added even when they have no text. Hidden elements are skipped. Each pair is compared with `collides()` (more than 2px of overlap on both axes). Pairs where one element contains the other are skipped, as are pairs inside an allow-overlap subtree. Any other collision produces `overlap: <describe a> overlaps <describe b>`, and `main()` prints it as `WARN step N: ...`. `describe()` names each element by `#data-presentation-id`, or by its `data-presentation-*` hook when it has no id, plus its visible text. The focused test 'reports an unmarked text collision with the step and both elements' sets up an unmarked collision between two overlapping Labels (coll-a and coll-b) on step 2 only. Judge B says the check leaves out the textless individual `[data-presentation-dot]` buttons. That doesn't decide the requirement. Footer.tsx renders every dot button inside that `<ol>`, and the sample's style.css lays the dots out in normal flow inside it (gap only, no positioning). So a dot that overlaps other text or chrome also overlaps the dots container, and the helper reports that as `[data-presentation-dots]`. Dots overlapping each other is not a case the criterion names. Comparison on each step: `main()` runs `diagnose` after every settled capture inside the step loop (inspect-presentation.mjs:142-151). `diagnose` builds a box for each visible element that has its own text, and for every chrome element in `chromeSel`, whether or not it has text (lines 56-76). It then compares every pair with `collides()` (lines 77-85). Only pairs where one element contains the other, or where an element is inside an allow-overlap subtree, are skipped. 2. Warning names the step and both elements: the output line is `WARN step N: overlap: <a> overlaps <b>` (line 150). `describe()` prints `#data-presentation-id`, or the element's `data-presentation-*` hook when it has no id, plus its visible text (lines 39-45). That counts as identifying the element under the guidance. 3. Focused test: 'reports an unmarked text collision with the step and both elements' sets up two overlapping, unmarked Labels (coll-a and coll-b) on step 2. It asserts exactly one warning matching `^WARN step 2: overlap: .*#coll-a.*#coll-b`, and per-step warning counts of [0,1,0]. 4. Textless chrome: the sample does render textless dot buttons (Footer.tsx:36-43), and they are not in `chromeSel` one by one. But the textless progress-indicator chrome is not dropped. The `<ol data-presentation-dots>` has no text, is in `chromeSel`, and gets its own box. Every dot is rendered inside that inline-flex `<ol>`, and the quoted CSS lays the dots out in normal flow with only a gap (style.css:73-90). So the container's box encloses each dot, and anything overlapping a dot by more than the tolerance also overlaps `[data-presentation-dots]`, which is reported under that stable hook. first_results.rationale: I'm ruling with judge B (pass). The three clauses hold. (1) Typed props: every public primitive exported from index.ts has an explicit typed interface. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use NodeProps (id: string, at?: At, className?: string, style?: CSSProperties, variant?: string, children?: ReactNode). Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use ArrowProps, AppearProps and SceneLayerProps. None is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, which is the fail trigger the guidance names for this clause. (2) Identity hooks cannot be overridden: MotionNode destructures a fixed set of fields and builds layoutId, data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and data-variant itself, with no caller spread on the rendered element. Arrow and SceneLayer set their data-presentation-* hooks directly. SceneLayer spreads only the caller's style object. Appear accepts no caller element props. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: `at` is used only by placement(); Box pulls `Icon` out and renders it as a child; `kind` and `tag` are used only to pick the hook value and the element; Arrow's from, to, bend, bidirectional, designW and designH go into path math and sizing. Judge A fails clause 1 because the interfaces are bespoke rather than inherited element props. The guidance's trigger for that clause is an untyped bag in place of the element's props, and it says typed primitives that apply hooks safely and strip kit-only props pass. A hand-written typed interface is not an untyped bag, so A's reason does not decide the requirement. Judge C says Box's `{...props}` after `kind="box"` lets a caller override data-presentation-node. Box's rest props are typed as NodeProps minus Icon and children, and NodeProps has no `kind` or `tag` field. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip likewise take only NodeProps, so TypeScript's JSX excess-property check rejects a caller passing `kind`. No source in the candidate passes it, so C's scenario is a hypothetical input the cited source does not produce. Also, layoutId and data-presentation-id are written inside MotionNode with no caller spread after them.

audit_results.rationale: This is a close call, but the quoted lines meet all three clauses. (1) Typed props: every exported node primitive declares an explicit interface. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use NodeProps or an extension of it. Arrow uses ArrowProps, Appear uses AppearProps and SceneLayer uses SceneLayerProps. None is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>, which is the fail trigger the guidance names. The guidance also says typed primitives that protect their hooks and strip kit-only props pass. The requirement wording 'the rendered element's props' could be read more strictly, as requiring the element's own prop type, but the guidance's fail trigger and pass phrase both turn on typed versus untyped. (2) Identity hooks: the rendered element gets layoutId, data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and data-variant from an object MotionNode builds itself (MotionNode.tsx:13-23), with no caller spread on the element. Arrow writes its data-presentation-* attributes directly with no caller spread. SceneLayer spreads only the caller's style object, which carries no hook. Appear takes no caller element props. Box and Label do pass `{...props}` after `kind=...`, but those props are typed as NodeProps, which has no `kind` or `tag` field. MotionNode is not exported from index.ts. A caller could override `kind` only by getting around the public prop types, and no quoted source does that, so this is a hypothetical input. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: MotionNode destructures kind, tag and at and never forwards them. Box pulls Icon out and renders it as a child. Arrow uses from, to, bend, bidirectional, designW and designH only for path math and sizing.

lines.text: ## Step 0 — tests and coverage already asserted

I read the focused scaffold, bootstrap, inspect, sample-scene, and verify-failure tests. The suite asserts scaffold anchor decisions, fresh/partial materialization, dependency declarations, verification failures, project-local screenshot generation and warning classes, and the sample’s outer-frame/ghost-card content. The tests do not exercise the public skill as a separate conversational actor. The reference sample’s automated inspection uses a wide viewport; its assertions do not establish narrow-view readability. The focused test files and their assertions are recorded in the acceptance run context. After exploration, the repository gates were run in the isolated scratch copy: npm ci, npm test (88 passed), npm run test:integration (35 passed), npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run verify; all passed. Summary: acceptance-automated-validation.md. This corroborates the manual observations but does not replace the coverage floor.
### AT-001 — create through the public skill and scaffold targets

- **Standalone mechanics exercised in scratch:** prediction: an empty standalone target resolves to its root and receives all three anchors; a generated route builds and opens. Observed: detect reported the scratch root and build/kit/index all missing; bootstrap created the app, kit, index, and local verification/inspection scripts; the package declared React, React DOM, Motion, Lucide, Vite, TypeScript, ESLint, and Playwright. The scaffold helper created acceptance-demo, the isolated production build succeeded, and AXI opened /acceptance-demo with a three-step scene, captions, controls, and the attribution link.

- **Partial monorepo mechanics exercised in scratch:** prediction: a monorepo with a valid build anchor at presentations/ resolves there, refuses unconfirmed writes, then adds only missing kit/index infrastructure after confirmation while preserving root and app files. Observed: detect returned target presentations/, build=true, kit=false, index=false. Bootstrap without --confirmed exited 2 and named that target; after confirmation it added the kit, index, and script files, preserved the existing build script, App.tsx, Vite config, and unrelated root README, and returned needsRouting=true. I wired the existing entry point from the shipped router template, created mono-demo, built it, and AXI opened /mono-demo successfully.

- The required interactive public-skill behavior was not independently exercised: asking one question at a time, honoring a partial-detail choice, presenting the monorepo target in conversation, obtaining the user's confirmation, and reporting its own build/render/visual checks. These require observing a separate skill actor and contingent replies; invoking the same skill as its own acceptance tester would not supply independent evidence. The fixture mechanics are not a substitute for that limitation.
### AT-002 — preserve presentations and scope a modification

- **Creation and preservation mechanics exercised in scratch:** prediction: registering a third presentation leaves the two existing entries/files intact and all routes resolve. Observed: created two entries alongside acceptance-demo; SHA-256 checks for its Talk.tsx and style.css remained unchanged. The app built, and AXI opened all three routes with the expected first-step title.

- The public skill's ambiguous-target listing, user's target selection, scoped content/style modification, and its verification report were not exercised by an independent conversational actor. These are named as a limitation, not treated as passed based on direct helper calls.
### AT-003 — interact with the reference scene

- The production build in the isolated app succeeded. The project-local helper captured all nine steps at 1440×900 and 390×844; no page or console errors were reported. AXI snapshots exposed nine progress buttons with step titles, the current title/caption, semantic active state, and the attribution link. Reviewed settled images for first, dense build, verification, and final reveal steps in wide and narrow views; AXI also captured the middle step in present mode. See the screenshot index and manifests under acceptance-screenshots/.

- Navigation observations: keyboard Right advanced 0→1; Space advanced 0→1; PageUp returned 1→0. Synthetic browser touch left swipe advanced 0→1 and right swipe returned 1→0. Progress direct-jump selected step 9 (index 8); ArrowRight remained at 8. At index 0 ArrowLeft remained at 0. Selecting the wide-view TOC entry “the build” from index 1 jumped to its first step, index 5. Its active entry exposed aria-current=step and data-presentation-active=true; the current progress button exposed aria-current=step.
- Focus behavior: a progress button for step 2 was focused while the active index was 5; ArrowRight left the index at 5 and kept focus on the button.

- Mode behavior: toggling on index 5 switched browse→present and back without changing index. In present mode the marker, title, and attribution remained; caption, TOC, nav, and progress dots were hidden. The brand slot was empty. Browse mode restored the caption, navigation, and TOC at wide width.

- Continuity and transitions: on the sample’s grouped htmp scene, the scene DOM node remained the same while its payload moved between beats; stable entity IDs continued and new IDs were added. A generated scratch transition fixture additionally moved a persistent entity, introduced a transient entity, and removed it on the next step. At 40 ms into exit, the transient remained mounted with opacity 0.758681 and an active 400 ms exit animation; the next entity’s entrance reported a 600 ms delay. This directly observed entering and departing motion.

- Canvas observations: the stage retained 880×380 dimensions at both viewports. AXI reported scale 0.644 wide and 0.407 narrow. Wide composition was readable. At narrow width, the composition did not reflow and remained inside the viewport, but fine labels were only a few pixels high. This tension is recorded in the assumptions ledger, not silently resolved.

- The default attribution read “made by and-scene”, linked to https://github.com/and-scene/and-scene, exposed its styling hook, and computed to 12px in the designed sample. No default top-left brand was present.

- A no-presentation-CSS scratch route rendered kit boxes without border, background, or shadow defaults. Its native button retained browser-default styling, and the kit supplied no theme. Scaffold package metadata contained no styling framework.
### AT-004 — failure and visual-warning repair loop

- **Warning detection exercised in a scratch fault fixture:** prediction: the project-local helper warns for unmarked overlap, indistinct active progress/TOC chrome, and undersized/browser-default attribution, but suppresses an explicitly allowed overlap. Observed: step 2 emitted the unmarked text-collision warning; each step emitted dot and TOC indistinct-active warnings plus 9px/default-link attribution warnings. Two labels under an allow-overlap subtree generated no overlap warning.

- The public skill's response to an injected build/browser failure, fixing the functional failure, repairing accidental collisions and chrome, rerunning verification, and reporting completion was not exercised by a separate skill actor. No repair result is claimed.
### Other approved scenarios exercised or limited

- The project-local helper ran at the default desktop size and at 390×844, settled all nine images, and retained capture timestamps and warning lists. Running it twice at the same output path rewrote a manifest with nine unique step files and new capture times. After helper completion, only the separately launched preview servers remained; those were stopped. The preview and inspection servers used 127.0.0.1.
- The helper warning fixtures exercised overlap exemption, dot and TOC active-state warnings, attribution warnings, and an unmarked collision. The normal wide sample returned zero warnings.

- The kit snapshot and bootstrap copy were byte-identical by recursive diff. Generated app builds established that typed scene payloads pass through the Presentation boundary without casts. The sample’s visible marker numbers ran in order 01 through 09.

- The normal npm run verify path passed with nine steps rendered without errors at 127.0.0.1. The integration suite also passed its fault cases for build failure, missing registration, out-of-order sample, console/page errors, failed transition, and preview cleanup. These are automated observations; the interactive skill repair loop remains unobserved.
- Human-only obligations: none; the test plan lists no HT-* items.
Four steps, one per seam, within the 1–8 cap:

1. **Registry parser / registration seam.** Prediction: a syntactically valid single-line registry remains usable. Observed: create registered a presentation into an empty presentations array; the result built into a valid multiline array. No finding.

2. **Dependency install decision / existing node_modules seam.** Prediction: --install calls npm even when node_modules already exists and declarations are already satisfied. Observed: an empty node_modules fixture and an npm shim recorded install in the fixture cwd; the helper reported installed=true. This verifies the invocation decision, not a real network installation. No finding.

3. **Sample scene reveal composition seam.** Prediction: no canvas-wide border appears before step 9; the final step adds the reveal. Observed: the step-7 screenshot contains no outer frame; step 9 contains the labeled reveal frame. No premature frame finding.

4. **Inspection output/process ownership seam.** Prediction: repeating inspection in the same project output path yields nine current screenshots and a fresh manifest without leaving its preview child running. Observed: nine unique step files, all capture timestamps later than their navigation timestamps; the inspection-owned preview exited. No finding.

The narrow inspection pass produced a false positive on every step: it reported overlap between the marker number and era label. AXI text-fragment rectangles show the glyphs do not overlap; the wrapped era element’s union box overlaps the number box. This is recorded as product defect P2 in acceptance-findings.md.

All run/setup errors and their exact excerpts/provenance are retained in scratch/acceptance-test/execution-errors.md. These were corrected tester or fixture commands, not application failures: wrong build cwd (ENOENT), an invalid monorepo fixture missing tsconfig (TS5083), missing python, two malformed scratch fixture patches, an unmatched-shell-quote attempt, a circular DOM value returned to AXI, stale AXI refs, an unsupported inspector --help flag, and an initially incompatible merge-tree option set. The successful reruns are recorded above.

The bundled current-head wait-ci script failed before querying because the installed gh does not expose baseRefOid. Its exact excerpt and provenance are recorded in acceptance-ci.md. A read-only PR query confirmed the tested head and one successful CodeRabbit status context, but also found the PR merge-conflicted at .validator/config.yml. This is an acceptance blocker.

- The public skill’s conversational question/answer, partial-detail, confirmation, ambiguous-target, scoped-modify, and agent-led repair workflows; no separate independent agent/user interaction was available in this no-human acceptance session.

- A separate skill actor responding to the verification fault cases and visual warnings by repairing the fixture and reporting completion; the automated fault suite passed, but agent-led repair was not independently observed.

- Nonstandard layouts beyond the valid partial-monorepo setup, such as a kit lacking the expected index.ts, an anchor deeper than the detector’s search depth, or a registry without a presentations array.

- Manual inspection of every screenshot pixel-by-pixel; all nine were captured and representative first, last, dense, and verification steps were reviewed at both widths. Remaining design question is the narrow-scale legibility trade-off.

scene-kit.rationale: The auditor's claim holds. The guidance says to judge the kit's ungrouped step transition together with the kit's entity primitives that render the persisting entity. It fails the criterion when a same-identity entity vanishes and reappears instead of morphing, and passes it only when the entity stays visible while it animates from its old state to its new state in place. Stage keys each scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id`, so two consecutive ungrouped steps mount separate scene instances. MotionNode carries a layoutId inside a shared LayoutGroup and can morph across scenes, but Arrow, also a kit entity primitive with an identity `id`, has no layoutId. Its path `d` interpolation only works while the same instance stays mounted, because `initial={false}` makes a newly mounted path start at its destination. So across an ungrouped transition, the new Arrow fades in from opacity 0 at its new geometry while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene. That is a crossfade between two separate copies, not a morph in place, so the pass verdict is defeated.

The guidance's fail trigger for that clause is an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown> used instead of the element's props. None of the primitives uses an untyped bag: NodeProps, ArrowProps, AppearProps and SceneLayerProps are explicit typed interfaces built from React types (CSSProperties, ReactNode).
